newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope at concert on eve of ordination anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Pope at concert on eve of ordination anniversary.

text.p: A relatively healthy looking Pope John Paul on Thursday attended a concert in his honour on the eve of the 50th anniversary of his ordination as a priest.
The concert, a performance of Georg Friedrich Handel's Messiah, was offered to the Pope by the Austrian government and performed by the Salzburg Camerata and the Mozartchor of Linz.
At the end of the 90-minute concert, the Pope read a brief address in which he thanked all those who had helped him in the past 50 years since his ordination.
The Pope, who underwent surgery earlier this month to remove his appendix, looked relatively healthy during the concert.
He stopped to shake hands with the musicians and some members of the crowd in the Vatican's huge modern audience hall as he left.

The Pope is to mark the anniversary of his ordination on Friday by celebrating a mass in St Peter's Basilica. It will be the first full-length public religious ceremony he has led since leaving hospital on October 15.
